ticket.title: ledger-verify reports zero and ledger-reconcile fails, both against the pre-migration ledger

task.title: ledger-verify reports zero and ledger-reconcile fails, both against the pre-migration ledger

events.description:
MEASURED 2026-11-08 in the suite root, after the migration moved every ticket to a file per ticket (ADR 0010):

  ticket files in .gaugeblock/storypole/tickets/   162
  duplicate keys among them                         0
  case-colliding keys among them                    0   (checked lower-cased, since the constraint is on
                                                         ticket_key_lower)

  storypole ledger-verify      exit 0   "0 events across 0 files: 0 unparsable, 0 duplicate / replay: 0 tasks"
  storypole ledger-reconcile   exit 1   "UNIQUE constraint failed: tasks.ticket_key_lower"

TWO SEPARATE FAULTS, same cause. Both verbs read the append-only `ledger.jsonl` that no longer exists as a source -
`ls .gaugeblock/storypole/` shows index.sqlite, ledger-archive, plans and tickets, and no ledger.jsonl. So:

  * `ledger-verify` finds nothing, replays nothing, and reports success. A green result is exactly wrong here: it is the
    command whose job is to detect a corrupt ledger, and it currently certifies an absent one. Anyone running it after
    the migration gets assurance about zero tickets while 162 exist.
  * `ledger-reconcile` fails on a UNIQUE constraint with no duplicate or case-colliding key in the data, so the fault is
    in the tool rather than the store - most likely replaying nothing and then inserting rows that are already present,
    without an upsert.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN ITS P3 SHAPE: these two commands are the integrity story for the ledger. `ledger-verify`
reporting zero is not a small inaccuracy - it is the specifically dangerous kind, because absence reads as health. It is
the same failure this session found four times elsewhere: a reader looking somewhere the truth no longer lives, and
reporting the resulting silence as a pass.

WHAT THE FIX MUST DECIDE: after ADR 0010 the source of truth is one file per ticket, so either these verbs read the
ticket files (and the archive for pre-migration history), or they are retired in favour of a verb that does. Keeping a
verb that replays a ledger nobody writes is how a suite ends up with a green check that proves nothing.
